item.title: Breathers across the Focusing-to-Defocusing Transition: From Diffraction-Like Dynamics to Talbot Carpets
item.description: arXiv:2611.08980v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We experimentally investigate fundamental unstable breather wave groups propagating across the transition from focusing to defocusing regimes. In hydrodynamics, this transition is realized through a rapid reduction in water depth over a short spatial interval. We demonstrate that the time-periodic Akhmediev breather develops a Talbot-like recurrence pattern in the defocusing regime, although only its initial stages are experimentally accessible. In contrast, the Peregrine breather exhibits qualitatively different behavior, characterized by oscillatory envelope dynamics. These oscillations can be understood as a purely linear phenomenon arising within the nonlinear Schr\"odinger framework when dispersion dominates over nonlinearity, as further confirmed by numerical simulations over extended propagation distances. The experimental observations agree closely with finite-depth nonlinear Schr\"odinger predictions across regimes with substantially different relative strengths of dispersion and nonlinearity. Our findings reveal a temporal analogue of diffraction and provide a foundation for exploring focusing-to-defocusing transitions in other nonlinear dispersive media.
item.dc:creator: Andrea Armaroli, Hung-Chu Hsu, Meng-Syue Li, Lili Kimmoun, Jie Zhang, Michel Benoit, Nobuhito Mori, Stefano Trillo, Amin Chabchoub

item.title: Continuum mean-field theory of spatiotemporal pattern formation in a three-state active Potts model
item.description: arXiv:2611.09180v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the spatiotemporal dynamics of a three-state active Potts model with a cyclic transition bias. Starting from microscopic Glauber-type dynamics, we derive macroscopic continuum field equations through a spatial mean-field approximation. Linear stability and weakly nonlinear analyses reveal that increasing the coupling strength induces a Hopf bifurcation, near which the critical amplitude dynamics is described by the complex Ginzburg--Landau equation. In the spatially homogeneous limit, the system exhibits limit-cycle oscillations and ordered states, with an intermediate regime of bistability bounded by a $\mathbb{Z}_3$-symmetric heteroclinic bifurcation. In two dimensions, the system sustains stable rotating spiral waves. Using perturbation theory based on one-dimensional traveling fronts, we semianalytically predict the curvature-dependent propagation velocity of circular fronts, as well as the rotational angular velocity and pitch of spiral waves. Finally, we compare the continuum model with discrete Monte Carlo simulations to clarify the role of thermal fluctuations and evaluate the validity of the mean-field approximation.
item.dc:creator: Yuta Tateyama, Songhao Yin, Hiroaki Ito, Hiroyuki Kitahata, Hiroshi Noguchi

item.title: Self-injection-locked dark-soliton Kerr optical frequency combs with high even-order normal dispersion
item.description: arXiv:2611.08848v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We numerically investigate dissipative dark-soliton (DDS) microcombs under the action of pure high even-order normal (HEON) dispersion in a microresonator with the self-injection locking (SIL). Pure 4th, 6th, 10th, and 14th-order normal dispersion can support DDSs formed by interlocked switching waves, directly excited through a SIL-based turnkey scheme without detuning sweeps. Compared to the pure 4th-order case, the switching-wave tail oscillation period increases and its decay rate decreases with the increase of the dispersion order. Although the overall comb bandwidth narrows, the number of non-pump comb lines above a common absolute power threshold increases. Furthermore, the feedback phase controls the DDS duty cycle and intracavity comb-line power distribution, while the increase of the pump power improves the estimated pump-to-comb output conversion efficiency.
item.dc:creator: Lei Shi, Rujiang Li, Shilong Liu, Dumitru Mihalache, Boris A. Malomed, Pengfei Li

item.title: A scaled TW-PINN framework for soliton solutions of the Korteweg--de Vries equation
item.description: arXiv:2611.09339v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Accurate approximation of soliton solutions of the Korteweg--de Vries (KdV) equation remains challenging for physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) due to localized wave structures, high-order spatial derivatives, nonlinear interactions between solitons, and difficulties in long-time prediction. In this work, we address these challenges using a scaling PINN framework to approximate KdV soliton solutions. The framework transforms the governing equation into a normalized form, approximates its solution using a PINN solver, and reconstructs the solution in the original variables through inverse scaling. We introduce scaling transformations and PINN solvers tailored to one- and two-soliton problems. For the one-soliton case, we employ a PINN solver that incorporates a traveling-wave coordinate to capture soliton propagation. For the two-soliton case, we employ a two-step training procedure for the PINN solver. The first step learns the individual soliton profiles and estimates their propagation speeds, while the second step uses the estimated speeds to construct traveling-wave coordinates in the PINN solver and approximate the full two-soliton solution, including nonlinear interactions. We also introduce soliton-informed sampling (SIS), which places additional collocation points around the soliton trajectories. Numerical results show that the scaling PINN framework accurately captures one-soliton propagation, resolves two-soliton interactions, and preserves soliton profiles during long-time extrapolation in both cases. An additional three-soliton experiment suggests the applicability of the proposed two-step training procedure to multi-soliton solutions.
item.dc:creator: Seungwan Han, Jiaxi Gu, Daniel Olmos-Liceaga, Jae-Hun Jung

item.title: Selection versus residuals: deep-learning solvers for the Dubreil-Jacotin-Long equation and application to mode-2 internal solitary waves
item.description: arXiv:2611.09498v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Neural solvers offer structural flexibility for the Dubreil-Jacotin--Long (DJL) equation of internal solitary waves, which also admits the trivial state, oscillatory wavetrains and broadened near-solutions. A solver must select the physical wave before resolving it. Turkington's variational principle selects the wave through the nonlinearity of the available potential energy (APE). An exact virial partition shows that every localized wave carries more kinetic energy than APE, so a quadratic APE would favour a broadened field. The nonlinear APE enhancement, $1.27$--$2.06\times$ for the computed waves, reverses this ordering, although the preferred width remains weakly selected. From a shared KdV-derived start, a constrained Deep Ritz objective recovers the mode-1 wave, whereas strong- and weak-form residual objectives, which vanish at every exact solution and therefore do not favour the physical wave over other roots, lose the prescribed APE within one descent round. The recovered wave is under-resolved because its residual is dominated by high-wavenumber error that the energy barely penalizes, and a residual refinement at exact APE then meets every acceptance criterion. Structurally excluding mode 1 from the trial space, we compute mode-2 waves on four stratifications. A computed wave core qualitatively reproduces the two-lobe structure observed on the South China Sea shelf. In the deep basin, the selected core misses the residual criterion, and residual refinement widens it with little change in the energy objective. The two resolved linear estimates suggest weaker relative mode-1 radiation at larger ratios of wave half-width to resonant wavelength.
item.dc:creator: Qiang Li, Yaoyin Zhang

item.title: Mode interaction in inclined-layer convection: a physical interpretation
item.description: arXiv:2611.09545v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We carry out a numerical investigation of the Oberbeck--Boussinesq equations in a fluid layer inclined against gravity. Equilibria containing different numbers of co-rotating rolls are computed. Mixed-mode branches connect branches containing states with four and six identical co-rotating rolls. These branches display two contrasting routes to reducing (or increasing) the number of rolls, one in which rolls disappear (or appear) and another route in which rolls merge (or split). These results are interpreted in light of the $(2,3)$ mode interaction scenario.
item.dc:creator: Zheng Zheng, Laurette S. Tuckerman, Tobias M. Schneider
